{{nihongo|'''Sasa Shrine'''|佐々神社}} is an {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=inner shrine}} (small shrine) in Otowa, {{ill|Iga, Mie|Q460820|qid=Q460820}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196}}. {{nihongo|'''Sasa Shrine'''|佐々神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Iga Province]].

== Commentary ==
In {{ill|Bud Abbott|Q23888|qid=Q23888}} (Kashō 3), Sasa Shrine, together with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aekuni Shrine}}, was among the earliest shrines in {{ill|Iga Province|Q1047128|qid=Q1047128}} to receive the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} of Junior Fifth Lower, showing high sacred status. Later, in {{ill|Codemasters|Q23901|qid=Q23901}} ({{ill|Jōgan|de|Jōgan|es|Jōgan|fa|جوگان|fr|Ère Jōgan|ia|Jogan|id|Jōgan|ja|貞観 (日本)|ko|조간 (연호)|ru|Дзёган|simple|Jōgan|sr|Џоган|tr|Jōgan|uk|Дзьоґан (ненґо)|zh|貞觀 (日本)|zh_yue|貞觀 (日本)|qid=Q1075635}} 15), it became Junior Fifth Upper. At this grant, Aekunitsu-no-Kami, previously of equal rank, was promoted to Senior Fifth Lower (becoming a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), and in {{ill|Pope John XXIII|ace|Paus Yohanes XXIII|af|Pous Johannes XXIII|als|Johannes XXIII.|am|ፓፓ ዮዓነስ 23ኛ|an|Chuan XXIII|ar|يوحنا الثالث والعشرون|arz|يوحنا التالت و العشرين|ast|Xuan XXIII|ay|Juan XXIII|az|XXIII İoann|bar|Johannes XXIII.|bcl|Papa Juan XXIII|be|Ян XXIII|be_x_old|Ян XXIII|bg|Йоан XXIII|br|Yann XXIII|ca|Joan XXIII|cdo|Gáu-huòng Ioannes 23-sié|ceb|Papa Juan XXIII|cs|Jan XXIII.|csb|Papiéż Jón XXIII|cy|Pab Ioan XXIII|da|Pave Johannes 23.|de|Johannes XXIII.|diq|Johannes XXIII|dsb|Jan XXIII.|el|Πάπας Ιωάννης ΚΓ΄|eml|Giuànn XXIII|eo|Johano la 23-a|es|Juan XXIII|et|Johannes XXIII|eu|Joan XXIII.a|fa|پاپ ژان بیست‌وسوم|fi|Johannes XXIII|fr|Jean XXIII|fur|Pape Zuan XXIII|fy|Jehannes XXIII|ga|Pápa Eoin XXIII|gd|Pàpa Iain XXIII|gl|Xoán XXIII, papa|gn|Huã XXIII|hak|Kau-fòng Ioannes 23-sṳ|he|יוחנן העשרים ושלושה|hr|Ivan XXIII.|hsb|Jan XXIII.|hu|XXIII. Ioannes|tt|Иоанн XXIII|uk|Іван XXIII|ur|جان بیست و سوم|vec|Papa Giovani XXIII|vi|Giáo hoàng Gioan XXIII|war|Papa Juan XXIII|wuu|若望廿三世|yo|Pópù Jòhánù 23k|zh|若望二十三世|zh_min_nan|Kàu-hông Ioannes 23-sè|zh_yue|聖若望廿三世|qid=Q23873}} ({{ill|Kanpyō (era)|Q1346292|qid=Q1346292}} 3) to Senior Fifth Upper (becoming the {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} of Iga Province), while Sasa-no-Kami was not promoted.

The lineage of Sasa-no-Kami is unknown. In general Sasa-no-Kami is identified with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yae-Kotoshironushi-no-Kami}}, but because its original sacred site was a {{ill|Himorogi|ar|هيموروغي|es|Himorogi|fa|هیموروگی|fi|Himorogi|fr|Himorogi|id|Himorogi|it|Himorogi|ja|神籬|ko|신리 (신토)|pl|Himorogi|pt|Himoragi|ru|Химороги|simple|Himorogi|sv|Himorogi|zh|神籬|qid=Q60587}} on Mt. Sasagatake (738 m), it is also said to be the summoned {{ill|mountain spirit|ja|山霊|qid=Q11471212}} of that mountain. Hayase Yasutarō’s theory identifies it with the deity worshiped at {{ill|Ōtori Shrine|ja|大鳥神社 (甲賀市)|qid=Q60988403|lt=Kōyama Shrine}} in Kōyama, Ōhara Village, {{ill|Kōka District, Shiga|fa|بخش کوکا، شیگا|ja|甲賀郡|ru|Кока (уезд)|tr|Kōka İlçesi, Shiga|zh|甲賀郡|qid=Q4227244}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Shiga|af|Shiga-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Shiga|ar|شيغا (محافظة)|az|Şiqa prefekturası|azb|شیقا اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Shiga|be|Сіга (прэфектура)|bg|Шига|bn|শিগা প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|br|Prefedelezh Shiga|ca|Prefectura de Shiga|cdo|Shiga-gâing|ce|Сига (префектура)|ceb|Shiga-ken|ckb|پارێزگای شیگا|cs|Prefektura Šiga|cy|Shiga (talaith)|da|Shiga-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Shiga|eo|Gubernio Ŝiga|es|Prefectura de Shiga|et|Shiga prefektuur|eu|Shiga (prefektura)|fa|استان شیگا|fi|Shigan prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Shiga|frr|Shiga (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Shiga|gl|Prefectura de Shiga|hak|Shiga-yen|he|שיגה (מחוז)|hr|Shiga (prefektura)|hu|Siga prefektúra|hy|Սիգա (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Shiga|ilo|Prepektura ti Shiga|it|Prefettura di Shiga|ja|滋賀県|jv|Préfèktur Shiga|ka|სიგის პრეფექტურა|ko|시가현|la|Shigaënsis|lt|Šigos prefektūra|lv|Sigas prefektūra|mk|Шига (префектура)|mn|Шига муж|mni|ꯁꯤꯒꯥ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|शिगा प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Shiga|my|ရှိဂခရိုင်|ne|सिगा|nl|Shiga (prefectuur)|no|Shiga (prefektur)|os|Сигæ|pl|Prefektura Shiga|pnb|ضلع شیگا|pt|Shiga|ro|Prefectura Shiga|ru|Сига|sco|Shiga Prefectur|se|Shiga prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Shiga|si|ෂිගා ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Shiga Prefecture|sk|Šiga (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Шига|su|Préféktur Shiga|sv|Shiga prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Shiga|tg|Устони Шига|th|จังหวัดชิงะ|tl|Prepektura ng Shiga|tr|Shiga|tt|Сига (префектура)|uk|Префектура Сіґа|ur|شیگا پریفیکچر|vi|Shiga|war|Shiga (prefektura)|wuu|滋贺县|zh|滋贺县|zh_classical|滋賀縣|zh_min_nan|Siga-koān|zh_yue|滋賀縣|qid=Q131358}}. ''History of Kōka District'' records that this deity (roughly equal to Sasa-no-Kami) was {{ill|invited|ja|射干|qid=Q11458542|lt=invited}} from a shrine in Kawai-gō and identifies it with {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, while ''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Isui Onko}}'' identifies it with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yae-Kotoshironushi-no-Kami}}, making confusion unavoidable.

''Isui Onko'' says the original site of Kōyama Shrine was “formerly at Sasagatake on the border of {{ill|Ōmi Province|ca|Província d'Ōmi|ckb|پارێزگای ئۆمی|cs|Provincie Ómi|de|Provinz Ōmi|es|Provincia de Ōmi|fa|ولایت اومی|fi|Ōmin provinssi|fr|Province d'Ōmi|gl|Provincia de Ōmi|hak|Ōmi-koet|id|Provinsi Ōmi|it|Ōmi|ja|近江国|ko|오미국|lt|Omio žemė|nl|Omi (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Ōmi|pt|Província de Ōmi|ru|Оми (провинция)|simple|Ōmi Province|sk|Ómi (provincia)|sr|Провинција Оми|tr|Ōmi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Омі|vi|Tỉnh Ōmi|zh|近江國|zh_min_nan|Ômi-kok|zh_yue|近江國|qid=Q843882|lt=Ōmi}}, but it burned in a field fire, and in the {{ill|Bunroku|ckb|بونرۆکو|es|Bunroku|fa|بونروکو|fr|Ère Bunroku|ia|Bunroku|id|Bunroku|ja|文禄|ko|분로쿠|ru|Бунроку|simple|Bunroku|sr|Бунроку|sv|Bunroku|tr|Bunroku|uk|Бунроку|zh|文禄|zh_yue|文祿|qid=Q1373039}} era was moved by local samurai Matsuo to the current location.” Matsuo is thought to be {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Matsuo Hyōgo-no-kami}}, who is said to have built a fort on Mikasa-yama in Kawai-gō. The Matsuo were local warriors of Matsuo in Kōka District, called “Lord Matsuo,” and a branch settled in Matsuo, Araki-gō, {{ill|Ahai district|Q11657437|qid=Q11657437}}, Iga Province.

Thus, the divine lineage of Sasa-no-Kami, deity of Sasa Shrine, is unknown and multiple theories coexist.
